title: Leprosy — Peripheral Nerve Involvement and Resulting Deformities
description: Flip each card to see the deformity caused by damage to that nerve in leprosy. M. leprae preferentially affects superficially located nerves (cooler skin temperature favours growth).

dialogs.answer: Claw hand — hyperextension at MCP joints, flexion at IP joints of 4th and 5th fingers. Loss of interossei and medial two lumbricals.

tips.front: Most commonly affected nerve in leprosy

dialogs.answer: Loss of thumb opposition (ape/simian hand). Thenar wasting. Inability to pinch between thumb and index finger.

tips.front: Test by asking patient to touch thumb tip to little finger tip

dialogs.answer: Foot drop — inability to dorsiflex the foot. High-stepping gait. Loss of eversion.
Plantar anaesthesia → painless trophic ulcers on sole of foot. Claw toes from loss of intrinsic foot muscles.

tips.front: Main cause of foot ulceration and disability in leprosy

dialogs.answer: Visibly and palpably thickened nerve — earliest and most commonly palpable enlarged nerve in leprosy examination.

tips.front: Look for it crossing the SCM — pathognomonic examination finding
